decision.summaryForCoordinator: ACCEPT. 19 attacks run, 19 refuted, 0 not sustained as a finding. 0 blockers, 0 MUST-FIX, 0 SHOULD-FIX. The land test here is the sharpest in the chain and it PASSES exactly. DR-G10 is the one gate whose live status cell is NOT 'OPEN': cell [7] reads 'HARD-BLOCKED pending selector refresh', and the artifact carries that string character for character. Every other gate-row join I have reviewed carries 'OPEN', so a template-following author would very likely have pasted it; this one did not, and 'HARD-BLOCKED' recurs 5 times across the reasoning rather than sitting isolated in the token field. The standing is internally coherent: OBL-SELECTOR-REFRESH remains leftoverDesign true, so the join declines to discharge the very thing the row is blocked on. Two vocabulary questions were checked per gate rather than assumed from siblings: OBL-G10-NAMED-CATALOG is correct because a g10 catalog artifact exists (unlike G24/G26), and live G10 v1 genuinely carries namedCorpusNotAuthored with values ordered-equal to the artifact's (unlike G26/G29). The v1-to-v2 delta is exactly one added obligation, OBL-G10-INPUT-CORPUS at leftoverDesign false, zero removals, zero standing changes, premise verified against the corpus's own bytes — 27 exactByteIntent occurrences, 23/23 states with stateNamed and source. D9 appears 14 times but the only two non-negations are the live class name 'D9/fault joins', which the namedCatalog role itself flags as a class name and not a code. DR-102's SATISFIED standing is preserved across 21 contexts; DR-G21 condition-4 and DR-133 are referenced only as remaining elsewhere. All 12 recordedInputs and every cited digest clean; HEAD 5d5d778; required-now 26.
